script.name: Gujarati script
notes: An abugida related to Devanagari but without the headline
Teach independent vowels, consonants, vowel signs, conjuncts, anusvara and punctuation progressively

features: vowel length and breathy phonation can distinguish words
romanisation is scaffolding, not a replacement for script

A1_design: Survival interaction, sound-script mapping, high-frequency phrases and core inflection.
A2_design: Daily independence through service encounters, plans, descriptions and practical messages.
B1_design: Connected narration, reasons, opinions, reported information and familiar problem-solving.
B2_design: Sustained argument, professional interaction, complex syntax and explicit stance.
C1_design: Advanced discourse organisation, register control, nuanced attribution, academic and professional communication.
C2_design: Precise lexical choice, implication and focus, rhetorical architecture, contextual idioms, sophisticated synthesis and flexible style.
register: તું is intimate and may be inappropriate upward
તમે is plural or respectful singular
honorific lexical choices such as પધારો mark respectful reception
formal prose favours explicit qualification and nominalisation where clarity benefits
pragmatics: particles and placement can mark focus
interpret address and requests through relationship and setting
idioms: interpret from context rather than word-for-word
distinguish living idiom, proverb and fresh metaphor
country_context: Use evergreen contexts from Gujarat including civic services, education, enterprise, literature and community life
Avoid treating all Gujarati speakers as culturally uniform

voice.notes: Use Gujarati voice for target-language text; keep English explanation in text.
